args.name: Practical berry propagation
args.function: Provide a feasible reusable method to propagate an existing berry plant into an additional rooted plant, if local conditions and actual available materials permit. Distinguish propagation from watering an existing plant.
args.conditions: At tick 17 commons-berry-0-0 was mature with stock 6, capacity 20 and soil moisture 0.65. The mastered watering contract says berries require moisture 0.6, so watering is not currently indicated. Other visible berry plants have stock 20. Propagation feasibility is unknown; use subsequent observations where relevant.
args.inputs: Identify whether actual berries, cuttings, tools, soil preparation or other materials are needed. I currently own six berries; do not assume any tools, seeds or vessels exist in my inventory.
args.costs: Specify realistic study time, labor, material consumption, site requirements and growth delays. Unknown costs should be investigated rather than waived.
args.effects: If feasible, implement an actionable propagation capability requiring actual learning and physical work, with explicit establishment conditions and delayed growth. Do not grant instant harvest, guaranteed survival or mastery. If infeasible, explain the limiting requirements.

candidates.function: Scoop a little river or shallow water by hand and pour it onto the soil plot of a rooted plant whose measured soil is drier than it needs.
Crush one of your own whole berries and rub its seeds free by hand, inspect a planting site, and sow the seeds in a small hand-loosened patch where they may root as a new plant und
Crack the hard casing of your own shelled material, such as hazelnuts, in 0.1 blocks with controlled impacts of your own hard blunt striker on a stable support, and take the loose

execution.progress: extract and inspect take one round; sowing is two paid one-round phases whose work, reserved seeds and patch persist; resume pays only the remaining phase after rechecks; rooting and growth run only in ordinary simulation.

details.costs: Study: 4 rounds, 0.2 energy each. extract: target your own whole untreated berry item; one unit per attempt (quantity 1): 1 round, 0.5 energy. inspect: x, y a site in reach and/or target your own item or a sowing patch in reach: 1 round, 0.2 energy. sow: target your seed lot; x, y a site in reach on open ordinary soil (.), moisture 0.3-1.2, waterlogging at most 0.1, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, fewer than 3 berry plants or patches being sown within 5 m. 2 rounds of 1 energy: loosen the patch, then place and cover the seeds; a loosened patch left by cancelled work needs only the second. pause, resume (workId), cancel: no energy. Refusals and failed rechecks cost nothing. No tool, vessel, water or soil is supplied.
details.effects: A whole berry unit (0.2 kg, food 8) is crushed: 0.01 kg of seeds (5 %, no food, no ageing) and 0.19 kg of pulp with all its food and age; both keep origin, harvest round and decay. The seeds of one unit are the one propagule the plant rules give one fruit unit; viability is unknown until something emerges. A unit whose parent is not a living berry plant has no represented seed: a paid failure, all pulp. Sowing moves the seeds from your inventory into the patch record, covered 5 mm deep in soil loosened 0.03 m. The patch gains establishment only from actual temperature (none at 6 C or below, full from 20 C), light, soil moisture (full from 0.6) and season; cold, darkness, drought or waterlogging stall it. At 12 a rooted seedling appears with no fruit (stock at most 4, the parent plant interval); fruit grows only under the existing growth rule; anyone may gather it. Watering a rooted plant is rooted-plant-watering. An unworked round pauses; cancel returns unsown seeds once and leaves loosened soil; death leaves them where you died. No reward or refund.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
